title: Adaptive stride pagination with popularity micro-index and tiered cache eviction for dashboard query API
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency and token cost for paginated dashboard queries (ad-hoc explorations + saved views) by introducing an adaptive stride pagination protocol backed by per-tenant popularity micro-indexes and a tiered eviction cache. This reduces fanout, unnecessary full-index scans, and cold-cache penalties for hot navigation patterns.

What we'll build:
- Stateless stride-based pagination token returned to client (opaque) encoding minimal cursor + stride hint.
- Server-side micro-index: compact per-tenant summaries (bloom-filter + min-sample quantiles) sharded by time-window to answer 'skip N' efficiently for common strides.
- Popularity tracker that updates micro-index weights per key path and periodically compacts hot slices into in-memory tier (tier-0 hot cache).
- Tiered cache eviction: per-tenant LRU for small-tenants + global segmented MRU/LFU policy for shared hot items; ephemeral TTLs for ephemeral exploratory queries.
- Client prefetch hints API: optional header x-rw-prefetch-hint with predicted next stride (used for safe background prefetch with bounded concurrency).
- Async hedging for long-tail pages: speculative second-request to alternate shard with request coalescing to reduce p99.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Micro-index size vs accuracy: using bloom + quantile sketches keeps memory low at cost of occasional fallback full scan; acceptable since fallbacks are counted and monitored.
- Stateful vs stateless cursor: keeping cursor minimal preserves routing and cacheability; stride hint enables efficient server-side prefetch without attaching large server state.
- Eviction complexity: tiered approach balances isolation for small customers and global efficiency for platform-wide hotspots.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests for micro-index correctness (edge cases: deletions, late-arriving events).
2) Feature flag rollout: start with read-only mode (index suggestions only), then safe prefetch (non-blocking), then active stride handling for 10% traffic, 50%, 100% with canary per-tenant.
3) Monitor key metrics (see below) and automated rollback on regressions.

Metrics to track:
- p50/p95/p99 query latency (overall + by tenant tier)
- cache hit rate (tier-0, per-tenant LRU hit rate)
- number of fallbacks to full scan per minute
- background prefetch bandwidth and CPU
- cost per query (token/CPU)

Open questions:
- Eviction thresholds tuning (memory budgets per pool) — requires offline sim on historical traces.
- How to surface prefetch opt-outs for privacy-sensitive tenants.
